arb-tax-decay.title: The longer it sits, the more the next swap pays
arb-tax-decay.lede: This pool prices staleness. Trade it twice in a row and the second swap is cheap; leave it alone and the price of going first climbs.
arb-tax-decay.liveLabel: the fee right now, given how long the pool has been quiet
arb-tax-decay.compareHint: Swap twice in quick succession: the second one is cheaper, because the pool was not stale.

priority-fee-tax.title: What you bid for position is what you pay
priority-fee-tax.lede: Racing flow bids for its place in the block. This pool reads that bid and charges for it.
priority-fee-tax.liveLabel: the fee for a swap at the current priority fee

curve.name: feeAtPriority
curve.xLabel: priority fee bid, gwei per gas

markout-fee.title: A fee that learns what its own flow is worth
markout-fee.lede: The pool grades each swap after the fact by whether the price kept moving its way, and prices the next one from the running average.
markout-fee.liveLabel: the fee at the toxicity this pool has measured

anti-snipe-ramp.title: Sniping the first block buys nothing
anti-snipe-ramp.lede: The pool opens at a punitive fee that decays to normal, and every cent of the difference goes to liquidity providers rather than the deployer.
anti-snipe-ramp.liveLabel: the fee at this point in the ramp

trading-calendar.title: A session, priced rather than enforced
trading-calendar.lede: The pool never stops quoting. Outside its trading session immediacy simply costs more, and the open and close are ramps rather than cliffs.
trading-calendar.liveLabel: the fee at this moment in the week

localDeploy.config: TradingCalendarHook.Config({openSecond: 13 hours + 30 minutes, closeSecond: 20 hours, rampSeconds: 30 minutes, sessionFee: 500, closedFee: 20_000, daysMask: 0x1F})

expiry-settle.title: Moving the settlement price gets dearer as it approaches
expiry-settle.lede: The fee ramps quadratically into maturity, so the print is most expensive to move exactly when moving it would pay most.
expiry-settle.liveLabel: the fee at this distance from maturity

step-curve.title: A quote that holds still
step-curve.lede: This pool prices in increments. Inside a band the quote is firm and a swap has no slippage at all; crossing one steps the price.

localDeploy.constructorArgs: IPoolManager(address(manager)), 2 * Q96, Q96 / 100, Q96 / 2, 1e18, 30, "Step Curve LP", "STEP-LP"

power-perp.title: Pick your exposure
power-perp.lede: A weighted geometric mean, so a provider chooses how much of the price move they want instead of always getting the square root of it.

yield-space.title: A pool that quotes a yield
yield-space.lede: The curve knows about the calendar: it converges to par at maturity on its own, so nobody has to be paid to arbitrage it there.

grid-ladder.title: A pool that quotes a bid and an ask
grid-ladder.lede: Two independent ladders, so the pool holds a market maker's position rather than a fee schedule. Buying always costs more than selling fetches.

epoch-rebalance.title: An index whose future is fixed before you deposit
epoch-rebalance.lede: The weight schedule is set at deployment and glides continuously, so the allocation on any future date is computable and no single block is worth racing to.

circuit-breaker.title: A pool that stops rather than being drained
circuit-breaker.lede: After a move larger than its threshold the pool halts swaps for a cooldown and resumes on its own. Withdrawals are never blocked.

oracle-band.title: A pool that will not be walked away from reality
oracle-band.lede: Swaps must clear inside a band around a signed reference price. Outside it the pool declines, and says by how much.

drawdown-cap.title: A cap on how far one address can move the price
drawdown-cap.lede: Each address gets a price-impact budget per epoch. Spend it and the pool declines the rest until the epoch turns.

reads.label: Ticks of impact left this epoch

depeg-shield.title: Fees that fight the depeg
depeg-shield.lede: The further the pool drifts from its peg, the more a swap that widens the gap pays, and the less one that closes it does.

reads.label: Fee to push away from the peg
Fee to push back toward it

dutch-clearing-launch.title: The pool will not sell below its schedule
dutch-clearing-launch.lede: A descending floor. Buy below it and the pool refuses; wait and the floor comes to you. Selling is never restricted.

localDeploy.config: DutchClearingLaunchHook.Config({startPriceX96: uint160(4 * Q96), floorPriceX96: uint160(Q96 / 2), startTime: uint64(block.timestamp), duration: 3600, buyIsZeroForOne: false})

flow-classifier.title: What this pool's flow is actually made of
flow-classifier.lede: The hook counts how many swaps arrive first in their block and how far each population moves the price, and publishes both. It changes nothing about the pool it measures.
flow-classifier.tryLabel: Swap and watch the numbers move

ratchet-floor.title: A floor that only moves up
ratchet-floor.lede: The pool refuses to trade below a floor that ratchets upward as the price rises and never falls back.
ratchet-floor.tryLabel: Try to sell through the floor

reputation-fee.title: Priced by who you are, without a signature
reputation-fee.lede: An agent registers the router it trades through, once. After that the pool prices its flow from an on-chain reputation score, with nothing for a router to forward.

retro-rebate.title: A volume rebate settled on-chain
retro-rebate.lede: Each swap skims into that epoch's pot. Once the epoch closes both the pot and the totals are final, so a claim is one division anybody can check and nobody can withhold.

form.name: epoch
form.label: Epoch to claim
form.hint: Must be a closed epoch: the running one is not final.

tenure-weighted-fees.title: Paid for staying, not for arriving
tenure-weighted-fees.lede: A slice of every swap goes to a pot shared by tenure, so capital that has been quoting for a month earns more than capital that arrived for one trade.

form.name: position
form.label: Position key
form.hint: keccak256(owner, tickLower, tickUpper, salt). Shown here so you can read what a position has earned.

liquidity-floor.title: A commitment the pool enforces
liquidity-floor.lede: Each position may withdraw freely down to the fraction it committed, and no further until the unlock. Nothing another provider does changes what you may take.

agent-budget.title: A spending limit the venue enforces
agent-budget.lede: A principal signs one budget for an agent; the agent signs each swap under it. The pool refuses anything past the cap, so the limit lives in the venue rather than in the agent's own code.

il-insurance.title: Cover the pool pays for itself
il-insurance.lede: A slice of every swap funds a cover fund. Withdraw for less than holding would have been worth and the fund pays the difference, up to what it actually holds.

vested-buy.title: Buy now, receive over time
vested-buy.lede: Buying through this pool delivers part of the fill immediately and vests the rest. The token itself is untouched: no transfer hooks, no allowlist.

top-of-block-auction.title: The first swap in a block is for sale
top-of-block-auction.lede: A searcher bids for the exclusive first slot in a future block and the pool keeps the money. Bid nothing and you simply cannot go first.

reads.label: Earliest block you may bid on

commit-reveal-dark.title: Commit now, trade one block later
commit-reveal-dark.lede: Every swap on this pool must have been committed to in an earlier block. Seeing an order stops being useful, because reacting to it would need a commitment made before you knew it existed. Commit below, watch the blocks count down, then reveal.

reserve-stable.title: A pool that pays you to fix it
reserve-stable.lede: Prices at parity with a signed spread. Take from the side that is running low and you pay a surcharge that goes into a stability fund. Take from the side that is too full and the fund pays you for the rebalance. Drain one side and watch the other direction turn into a rebate.

tick-harberger.title: Buy the right to price this range
tick-harberger.lede: Every price level is worth something different to trade at, and one pool-wide fee says otherwise. Name what the range holding the price is worth, pay rent on your own number, and set the fee inside it. Anybody can take it off you at the number you named, which is what keeps the number honest.

stream-dca.title: A standing order that buys more when the price falls
stream-dca.lede: Dollar-cost averaging spends the same money whether the asset halved or doubled. This commits to growing the position by a fixed amount each period instead, so a cheaper price means a larger buy and a dearer one means a smaller buy or none. Open a stream, move the pool, and watch the next buy resize itself.

block-reversal.title: The leg that closes a sandwich is the one that pays
block-reversal.lede: This pool never asks who is trading. It records where the price stood when the block opened and charges any swap that moves it back, in proportion to how much of the block's move it is unwinding. Push the price one way, then try to come back and watch the quote change.
